content.arguments:
{"command":"$p = (Resolve-Path 'scripts\core\BattleManager.gd'); $t = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($p)
$eol = if ($t.Contains("`r`n")) { "`r`n" } else { "`n" }
$summ = @'
func _create_summ_card(sname: String, sid: String) -> Panel:
	# 紧凑竖排卡（图标上、名字下）：5 列 × 2 行一屏放下 10 个召唤师技能，无需滚动
	var card = Panel.new()
	card.name = "SummCard_" + sid
	card.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(88, 78)
	card.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	card.add_theme_stylebox_override("panel", UiKit.skin_card(SEL_SUMM_COLOR, false, 0.72))
	var col := VBoxContainer.new()
	col.set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
	col.alignment = BoxContainer.ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	col.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 2)
	col.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
	card.add_child(col)
	var glyph = SelectArt.SummonerGlyph.new(sname, 30)
	glyph.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_CENTER
	col.add_child(glyph)
	var lbl = Label.new()
	lbl.text = sname
	lbl.horizontal_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	lbl.vertical_alignment = VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	lbl.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_SM))
	lbl.add_theme_color_override("font_color", SEL_TEXT)
	lbl.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
	col.add_child(lbl)
	card.gui_input.connect(_on_summ_card_clicked.bind(sid, sname, card))
	card.gui_input.connect(_on_summ_preview_input.bind(sname))
	card.mouse_entered.connect(_on_card_hover.bind(card, true, SEL_SUMM_COLOR))
	card.mouse_exited.connect(_on_card_hover.bind(card, false, SEL_SUMM_COLOR))
	card.mouse_entered.connect(_on_summ_hover.bind(sname, sid, card, true))
	card.mouse_exited.connect(_on_summ_hover.bind(sname, sid, card, false))
	return card
'@.Replace("`n", $eol)
$n = [regex]::Replace($t, '(?s)func _create_summ_card\(sname: String, sid: String\) -> Panel:.*?\r?\n\treturn card\r?\n', $summ.Replace('$','$$'))
if ($n -ne $t) { 'summ card rewritten' } else { 'summ card MISS' }
$t = $n
$row = @'
func _build_row(idx: int, item_id: String) -> PanelContainer:
	# 紧凑装备卡（序号/名称/价格/上下调序）：6 张横排一屏放下，无需滚动
	var item: Dictionary = ItemDatabase.get_item(item_id) if item_id != "" else {}
	var nm := str(item.get("name", item_id))
	var cost := int(item.get("cost", 0))
	var card := PanelContainer.new()
	card.name = "BuildRow_%d" % idx
	card.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0, 116)
	card.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	card.add_theme_stylebox_override("panel", UiKit.skin_chip(UiKit.C_PANEL_EDGE, 0.8, 10))
	var v := VBoxContainer.new()
	v.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 2)
	v.alignment = BoxContainer.ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	card.add_child(v)
	var idx_lab := _sel_label("%d." % (idx + 1), _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_XS), SEL_GOLD, false)
	idx_lab.horizontal_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	v.add_child(idx_lab)
	var name_lab := _sel_label(nm, _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_XS), SEL_TEXT, false)
	name_lab.horizontal_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	name_lab.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	name_lab.clip_text = true
	v.add_child(name_lab)
	var price_lab := _sel_label("%d金" % cost, _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_XS), SEL_GOLD, false)
	price_lab.horizontal_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	v.add_child(price_lab)
	var btns := HBoxContainer.new()
	btns.alignment = BoxContainer.ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	btns.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 4)
	v.add_child(btns)
	var up := _sel_btn("↑", UiKit.C_TEAM0, false, Vector2(38, 26))
	up.name = "BuildUp_%d" % idx
	up.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_SM))
	up.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_CENTER
	up.disabled = idx <= 0
	up.pressed.connect(_on_build_move.bind(idx, -1))
	btns.add_child(up)
	var down := _sel_btn("↓", UiKit.C_TEAM0, false, Vector2(38, 26))
	down.name = "BuildDown_%d" % idx
	down.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_SM))
	down.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_CENTER
	down.disabled = idx >= sel_build_ids.size() - 1
	down.pressed.connect(_on_build_move.bind(idx, 1))
	btns.add_child(down)
	return card
'@.Replace("`n", $eol)
$n2 = [regex]::Replace($t, '(?s)func _build_row\(idx: int, item_id: String\) -> PanelContainer:.*?\r?\n\treturn row\r?\n', $row.Replace('$','$$'))
if ($n2 -ne $t) { 'build row rewritten' } else { 'build row MISS' }
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($p, $n2)","description":"Rewrite summon card and build card widgets"}

And panel at... wait build panel inside right_body; sizes 129x145 weird. Likely select_ui root is not scaled/full-rect in headless default (display size 2400x2400?), and select UI measured in a scaled container (UiKit scale). Anyway panel 129 wide → 6 cards 100 wide each overflow.

Wait first_card=(100,153): card min height 116 but reported 153? Because VBox content grows. And width 100.

The parent panel 129 wide is suspicious — maybe the right column is narrower than expected in this scaled UI, or measurement at t=120 but panel still not laid out because panel visible false earlier then tab pressed at t=15, so visible.

Hmm panel=(129,145) but rows belong to panel; panel width should be 520 in design scaled.

If actual right panel width is 129 in this environment, previous VBox rows (0 width, expand) fit; new 6-across cards (min 100 each = 600) overflow massively.

Since design width unknown, safer layout: 3 cards per row (2 rows) using GridContainer columns=3; card min width ~0 → 3*100=300 fits even in narrow; height 2*153=306 — may overflow vertically if panel short.

Alternatively keep 2 rows × 3 with smaller cards (height ~110).

But actual runtime is user's editor with display 1920-ish? UiKit likely scales relative to design resolution; measured 2400x2400 headless artifact (portrait?). Hmm.

Let me measure more: right_body size, right panel size, and total select root size. Also `_sel_fs` scaling. Print `root.size`, `right_body`, `right`, tabs etc. Need to know layout to choose columns.

Quick probe: print sizes of SelectRoot, SelectRightBody, sel_summ_panel, sel_build_panel, and the ScrollContainer `SelectSummScroll`(472 wide) — wait summ_scroll width 472 fits within right_body presumably ~520 ✓ so right body IS ~520 wide. But build panel says 129?? Contradiction: build panel is inside right_body same parent as summ panel. Unless `panel` found by find_child returned something else (e.g., "SelectBuildPanel" inside another node?).

Actually `root.find_child("SelectBuildPanel", true, false)` returns the right panel; but maybe `sel_summ_panel` was made hidden and build panel visible; sizes should reflect 520.

Wait panel.size (129,145) might be before layout because we called `_on_right_tab_pressed("出装")` at t=15, which calls `_rebuild_build_panel()` — that creates rows; layout next frame. Hold on: summ_scroll size (472,164) is not 520*0.25=130. So scale differs per widget? Unclear.

Maybe there are two SelectSummScroll? No.

Possibly at t=15, select UI root exists but the right column layout still default sizes; the t=15 measurement (summ) got 472 from explicit min width? summ_scroll has no explicit width; 472 could come from grid min width 5*88+4*8=472 ✓ — that's content min width, not available width! So summ_scroll width = min content width because parent layout not applied → layout broken in headless? Then its size 472×164 = content min. So no conclusion about fit; cards min 88*5=472 ≤ 520 designed width ✓ but if actual right body width < 472 → horizontal overflow clipped (scroll disabled!) — risky.

For build: card min width ~100 → 6 cards=600 > 520 → definitely overflow. So 6-across too wide. Use 3 columns × 2 rows (GridContainer) with card min width 0 but content ~100 → 3*100=300 ✓ safe; height 2*153=306 — panel height? maybe ~400 available; plus scheme 92 + bottom 40 = 438 — might overflow vertically.

Alternative: 6 slots as single row but compact horizontally: remove ↑↓ buttons from each card, use click-to-select + swap interaction? I'll go GridContainer columns=3 for build rows (type change from HBoxContainer to GridContainer), cards min (0,112) expand fill.

Vertical fit uncertain but reasonable.

For summon cards min 88: 5*88+32=472. If actual right column narrower (e.g., 400), overflow. Reduce to 4 columns? 4*88+24=376 ✓ safer; rows: 10/4 = 3 rows = 3*78+16=250 tall. Hmm larger height but fine.

Let me measure actual right body width to be sure: probe print `SelectRightBody.size` and `SelectSummPanel.size` after settle. If width ~520 → fine.

Do quick probe with only sizes, then adjust build grid.

content.arguments:
{"command":"$p = (Resolve-Path 'scripts\core\BattleManager.gd'); $t = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($p)
$eol = if ($t.Contains("`r`n")) { "`r`n" } else { "`n" }
$body = @'
	var v := VBoxContainer.new()
	v.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 3)
	v.alignment = BoxContainer.ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	card.add_child(v)
	var top := HBoxContainer.new()
	top.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 3)
	v.add_child(top)
	var idx_lab := _sel_label("%d." % (idx + 1), _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_XS), SEL_GOLD, false)
	idx_lab.vertical_alignment = VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	top.add_child(idx_lab)
	var name_lab := _sel_label(nm, _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_XS), SEL_TEXT, false)
	name_lab.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	name_lab.vertical_alignment = VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	name_lab.clip_text = true
	top.add_child(name_lab)
	var price_lab := _sel_label("%d金" % cost, _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_XS), SEL_GOLD, false)
	price_lab.vertical_alignment = VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	top.add_child(price_lab)
	var btns := HBoxContainer.new()
	btns.alignment = BoxContainer.ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	btns.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 4)
	v.add_child(btns)
	var up := _sel_btn("↑", UiKit.C_TEAM0, false, Vector2(40, 26))
	up.name = "BuildUp_%d" % idx
	up.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_SM))
	up.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_CENTER
	up.disabled = idx <= 0
	up.pressed.connect(_on_build_move.bind(idx, -1))
	btns.add_child(up)
	var down := _sel_btn("↓", UiKit.C_TEAM0, false, Vector2(40, 26))
	down.name = "BuildDown_%d" % idx
	down.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_SM))
	down.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_CENTER
	down.disabled = idx >= sel_build_ids.size() - 1
	down.pressed.connect(_on_build_move.bind(idx, 1))
	btns.add_child(down)
	return card
'@.Replace("`n", $eol)
$n = [regex]::Replace($t, '(?s)func _build_row\(idx: int, item_id: String\) -> PanelContainer:.*?\r?\n\treturn card\r?\n', ('func _build_row(idx: int, item_id: String) -> PanelContainer:' + $eol + '	# 紧凑装备卡（序号/名称/价格 + 上下调序）：3 列 × 2 行一屏放下，无需滚动' + $eol + ($body -replace '\$','$$')))
if ($n -ne $t) { $t = $n; 'card compacted' } else { 'compact MISS' }
# 卡片最小高度改小
$t = $t.Replace('	card.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0, 116)', '	card.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0, 84)')
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($p, $t)
$a = Start-Process -FilePath (Resolve-Path '.cache\godot47.exe') -ArgumentList '--headless','--path','.','res://devfx27/probe.tscn','--quit-after','400' -PassThru -RedirectStandardOutput 'devfx27\p5.out' -RedirectStandardError 'devfx27\p5.err'
$d = $a.WaitForExit(150000); if (-not $d) { $a.Kill(); "TIMEOUT" }
Get-Content devfx27\p5.out | Select-String -Pattern '^L ' | ForEach-Object { $_.Line.Trim() }
"=== err ==="
Get-Content devfx27\p5.err | Select-String -Pattern 'Parse Error|SCRIPT ERROR' | Select-Object -First 6 | ForEach-Object { $_.Line.Trim() }","description":"Compact build cards and retest","timeoutMs":250000}

Layout: `bottom` HBox (h=300) contains left panel + mid + right? Let's read a bit before 2990 to see bottom's children (left summary, mid, right). Also `page` is VBox: header, main, bottom.

The right column (520) includes tabs + body + btn_row(92). Moving buttons to sides means: place 换英雄/返回大厅 at left edge and 开始游戏 at right edge, floating outside the right panel (e.g., in bottom row's left side or as overlay anchored bottom-left/bottom-right).

Simplest robust approach: create a bottom action bar as an overlay Control on `page` (or root), anchored to full rect with two side containers:
- Left: 换英雄 + 返回大厅 (horizontal, anchored bottom-left with margin)
- Right: 开始游戏/确定选择 (anchored bottom-right)
Then remove btn_row from `right` VBox so right body gets full height (more room for build/summon).

Check whether the bottom HBox has left area occupied by other content (left summary panel) — buttons at bottom-left may overlap left panel. Better: anchor buttons vertically centered on left/right screen edges? "移到两边" = to both sides.

But overlap risk: left panel at bottom-left. Place buttons at bottom edge outside panels: bottom HBox is 300 tall at bottom; below it maybe nothing. The screen page: header + main + bottom(300). Buttons 92 tall could go at very bottom row spanning full width: left cluster at left, confirm at right. That would be a new HBox added to page after bottom, height ~92 → takes vertical space again (but full width, so right panel unaffected; right panel body gets to use its area).

Actually current btn_row is inside right VBox so it consumed 92 of right column; moving it to a full-width bottom row frees the right column 92px (good) and buttons sit at screen's left/right edges.

Implement:
1. Remove `btn_row` creation/append from right; instead create `action_row := HBoxContainer.new()` added to `page` (after bottom) with custom_minimum_size (0, 84), containing: 换英雄, 返回大厅 on left; spacer expand; 开始游戏 on right. 180+180+spacer+340 → fits 1920 (and 1280: 180+180+340=700 ✓).

But wait page height: header + main + bottom 300 + action 84 may exceed available → bottom row might clip. Right column body height reduces though.

Alternative: overlay anchored bottom-left/bottom-right of `page` without consuming layout: create Control overlay inside `page`? Containers ignore anchors; but we can add buttons as children of `sel_pick_layer`? That layer is hidden in stage 2.

Better: use a separate CanvasLayer-like overlay Control added to root (SelectRoot) with PRESET_FULL_RECT and mouse_filter ignore, containing two HBoxes anchored bottom-left and bottom-right. This overlay sits above panels, doesn't affect layout. Buttons at screen bottom corners. Risk: overlapping left/right bottom panels (left team list bottom? right panel bottom edge). Place with margins: bottom-left at y = bottom - 96 - 12; but panels occupy bottom 300 → buttons would overlap panels' lower left area. Overlapping the panel = "blocking" again.

Hmm. Best: allocate a dedicated full-width action strip at the very bottom of page, below bottom HBox → no overlap; bottom HBox shrinks? No—VBox total: header+main+bottom(300)+strip(84) might exceed; then containers shrink main.

Let me inspect page structure heights and viewport to judge. Read page creation and header/main part (2850-2995).

{"command":"$p = (Resolve-Path 'scripts\core\BattleManager.gd'); $t = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($p)
$eol = if ($t.Contains("`r`n")) { "`r`n" } else { "`n" }
function Rep([string]$a, [string]$b, [string]$tag) { if ($script:t.Contains($a)) { $script:t = $script:t.Replace($a, $b); "OK $tag" } else { "MISS $tag" } }
# 1) 按钮行从右栏移除，改到底部两端
Rep ('	var btn_row := HBoxContainer.new()' + $eol + '	btn_row.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0, 92)' + $eol + '	btn_row.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 0)' + $eol + '	right.add_child(btn_row)') (@'
	# 两侧操作区：换英雄/返回大厅在左，确定/开始在右（不再占用右栏，避免挡住召唤/出装面板）
	var side_left := VBoxContainer.new()
	side_left.name = "SelectSideLeft"
	side_left.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(190, 0)
	side_left.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_CENTER
	side_left.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 10)
	bottom.add_child(side_left)
	bottom.move_child(side_left, 0)
	var side_right := VBoxContainer.new()
	side_right.name = "SelectSideRight"
	side_right.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(190, 0)
	side_right.size_flags_vertical = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_CENTER
	side_right.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 10)
	bottom.add_child(side_right)
'@).Replace("`n", $eol) 'move buttons out'
# 2) 各按钮挂到两侧 + 尺寸调整
Rep '	leave.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_MD))' '	leave.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_SM))' 'leave font'
Rep '	leave.pressed.connect(_on_select_leave)' '	leave.pressed.connect(_on_select_leave)' 'noop'
Rep ('	sel_back_btn = _sel_btn("换英雄", UiKit.C_PANEL_EDGE, false, Vector2(180, 92))') '	sel_back_btn = _sel_btn("换英雄", UiKit.C_PANEL_EDGE, false, Vector2(190, 86))' 'back size'
Rep ('	sel_back_btn.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_MD))') '	sel_back_btn.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_SM))' 'back font'
Rep ('	btn_row.add_child(sel_back_btn)' + $eol + '	btn_row.add_child(leave)') ('	side_left.add_child(sel_back_btn)' + $eol + '	leave.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(190, 86)' + $eol + '	side_left.add_child(leave)') 'attach left'
Rep ('	select_confirm_btn = _sel_btn("✔  开始游戏", UiKit.C_GOLD, true, Vector2(340, 92))') '	select_confirm_btn = _sel_btn("✔  开始游戏", UiKit.C_GOLD, true, Vector2(190, 100))' 'confirm size'
Rep ('	select_confirm_btn.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_LG))') '	select_confirm_btn.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", _sel_fs(UiKit.FS_SM))' 'confirm font'
Rep ('	btn_row.add_child(select_confirm_btn)') '	side_right.add_child(select_confirm_btn)' 'attach right'
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($p, $t)","description":"Move action buttons to screen sides"}

## Critical Context
- **Another process/session concurrently edits this project** (recent edits: `ai/hero_brains/*.gd`, `ai/perception/AiPerception.gd`, `scripts/core/BattleManager.gd`, `Minion.gd`, `SfxManager.gd`, `UI_Manager.gd`, `NetClientBattle.gd`; `_probe_hitch.gd` at repo root). Re-check mtimes/parse before export; never delete their `_probe_*.gd` files; user's Godot editor is open on `battle.tscn`.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Working Principles (user-mandated, 最高优先级)

用户时间与预算有限，**每个任务都必须为省时间/省 token 服务**：

- **最短路径**：只为当前任务做最小必要改动；不顺手重构、不新增无关文件、不写长篇注释或文档。
- **省 token 的读法**：先用 grep/glob 定位，再带 offset/limit 定点读；禁止重复整文件读取或整文件回显；改动优先用 edit，不要重写大文件。
- **少开 agent**：默认由 Lead 单独完成。只有当任务可拆成互不依赖的大块、且并行确实更快时才用 teammates；subagent 的上下文同样是成本。
- **验证从简**：本项目无测试套件，只做必要的最小验证（如 GDScript 语法/加载检查），不跑完整试玩流程，除非任务明确要求。
- **输出精简**：结论先行，只列改动点与验证结果，不复述代码。
- **任务完成必须弹 Windows 通知**：每次交付结束前执行
  `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\dev\notify.ps1 -Title "HonorKing · <任务名>" -Message "<一句话结果>"`
  （脚本已就绪，失败会静默降级，不阻断交付）。

## Project Overview

HonorKing — a 3D MOBA game built with **Godot 4.5** (Forward Plus renderer). All game logic is written in **GDScript**. The game simulates a 5v5 Honor of Kings-style match: one player-controlled hero plus 4 AI teammates versus 5 AI enemies across a three-lane map with jungle, turrets, and epic monsters.

## Development Commands

- **Run the game**: Open `project.godot` in the Godot 4.5 editor and press F5, or run `godot --path .` from the project root.
- **No tests, no build step**: There is no test suite or CI. The only way to verify changes is to run the game in the Godot editor.

## Architecture

### Autoloads (Globals)

Defined in `project.godot` → `[autoload]`. These singletons are available everywhere without `load()`:

| Autoload | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Config` | `scripts/core/Config.gd` | Constants: `MAP_SIZE=120`, `Team` enum (`PLAYER=0, ENEMY=1, NEUTRAL=2`) |
| `ItemDatabase` | `assets/ItemDatabase.gd` | All item definitions, synthesis trees, recommended build paths, `get_item()`, `can_build()`, `get_synthesis_cost()` |
| `SkillDatabase` | `assets/SkillDataBase.gd` | All skill definitions (hero skills + summoner spells), `get_skill()` |
| `GameManager` | `scripts/core/GameManager.gd` | Stub — currently empty (`_ready` and `_process` are no-ops) |
| `UiManager` | `scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd` | Comprehensive UI: skill icons, shop, kill feed, hero detail panel (C key), target info, death recap, buff panel, damage/gold/heal popups |
| `CollisionSystem` | `scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd` | Per-frame entity pushback to prevent overlapping (heroes ← → turrets, minions ← → turrets excluded) |

### Core Scripts (`scripts/core/`)

- **`BattleManager.gd`** — The central game controller (`class_name BattleManager`). Handles:
  - Map creation (ground planes, lane planes, river, high-ground circles)
  - Hero select UI → game start flow
  - Player hero + AI hero creation (one of each role: assassin/mage/marksman/warrior/support)
  - Turret, jungle camp, wall/bush placement
  - Minion wave spawning (3 lanes × 2 teams, with growth tables, siege/super/dragon minion variants)
  - Epic monster timers (Tyrant at 4min, Dragon at 4min)
  - Economy systems: kill/assist gold, tower gold, lane gold sharing, natural gold/exp, jungle item rules, support item rules
  - Input handling: left-click attack order, right-click move, raycasting for ground/target selection
  - Camera: follows player hero, minimap drag/jump override
  - Win condition: crystal destruction → game-over screen
  - Hero configs: `hero_configs` dictionary with base stats for all 17 heroes

- **`EntityDatabase.gd`** — Stub (empty `_ready`/`_process`).

- **`CameraController.gd`** — Standalone camera script (attached to a Camera3D), follows a `@export var target`. Currently unused — BattleManager controls the camera directly.

- **`MapGenerator.gd`** — Alternative map generator (creates a simpler 60×60 grass + river). Not used in the main game; BattleManager has its own `_create_map()`.

- **`CollisionSystem.gd`** — See Autoloads above.

### Entity Hierarchy (`scripts/entities/`)

All entities inherit from **`GameEntity`** (`class_name GameEntity extends CharacterBody3D`):

```
GameEntity
├── Hero (player & AI champions)
├── Turret (defensive structures)
├── Minion (lane creeps)
├── JungleMonster (neutral camps + epic monsters)
├── Bullet (projectile for ranged attacks and skill shots)
├── LinearBullet (directional projectile variant)
├── Wall (terrain obstacle)
├── Bush (stealth zone)
├── HealthPack (regen pickup)
├── TeleportZone (teleport pad)
└── prw (unidentified entity)
```

**`GameEntity`** provides:
- Base stats: `health`, `max_health`, `attack`, `armor`, `magic_resist`, `move_speed`, `attack_range`, `attack_speed`, `body_radius`, `level`
- State effects: slow, stun, knockup, freeze, suppress, silence, grievous wounds
- Shield system (`shield_remaining`/`shield_timer`)
- Marker system for stacking passives (e.g., Zhen Ji freeze, Angela burn, Marco Polo stacks)
- Damage calculation: `take_damage()` with armor/MR reduction formula (`resistance / (resistance + 602)`), penetration, crit detection
- Hunt DoT system (jungle item burn)
- Lifesteal application (physical and magical, with grievous wounds reduction)
- Death handling: `die(killer)` → signals, gold/exp distribution, buff transfer
- Kill assist detection (nearest enemy hero within 12 units)

**`Hero`** (`scripts/entities/Hero.gd`, ~2150 lines) — The largest and most complex class:
- **Stats**: base stats + role-based growth per level (tank/warrior/assassin/marksman/mage/support)
- **Equipment**: 6-slot inventory, `buy_equipment()` with component synthesis, `_apply_equipment_bonuses()` recalculates all stats from items, 100+ unique item passive/active effects
- **Skills**: 3 hero skills + summoner spell + recover, each with cooldowns, mana costs, charge/restore system, upgrade via Ctrl+key or auto-level
- **Hero-specific logic**: Each hero has hardcoded special behavior in `_physics_process()` (Arthur passive heal + W shield rotation, Donghuang orbs, Li Bai sword auras, Zhang Fei transformation + mana, Lanling stealth, Taiyi Q channeling)
- **Combat**: auto-attack with bullet spawning (ranged) or instant (melee), crit, on-hit effects from 20+ items
- **Input**: WASD movement, right-click move orders, left-click attack orders, skill hotkeys 1-3, summoner spell key, item actives (keys 6-0, V, =, -)
- **Post-game stats**: `damage_dealt_to_heroes`, `damage_taken_from_heroes`, `healing_done`, `cc_duration_dealt`, `turret_damage`, `jungle_gold`, `last_hits`, `gold_history`

**Other entity notes**:
- `Bullet.gd` / `LinearBullet.gd` — Projectiles with speed, damage, pierce, slow, red buff burn, team affiliation
- `Turret.gd` — Auto-attacks nearby enemies, has outer/inner/high/crystal tiers with different stats
- `Minion.gd` — Follows waypoints along lanes, attacks enemies in range
- `JungleMonster.gd` — Has `activity_radius` (leash range), `buff_type` for red/blue buff
- `Wall.gd` / `Bush.gd` — Static collision/stealth volumes
- `HeroAI.gd` — AI controller for bot heroes (attached as child of Hero)

### Asset Scripts (`assets/`)

- **`ItemDatabase.gd`** — Massive dictionary of all equipment items with: name, tier (1-4), cost, stat bonuses, `requires` (synthesis components), `passive`/`active` descriptions, category tags. Key functions: `get_item(id)`, `can_build(id, owned)`, `get_synthesis_cost()`, `get_synthesis_tree()`, `get_recommended_items(role)`.
- **`SkillDataBase.gd`** — Dictionary of all skills (hero abilities + summoner spells). Each skill defines: `type` (0=targeted, 1=AoE, 3=linear, 4=dash, 6=shield), `cooldown`, `mana_cost`, `cast_range`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, etc.
- **`Skill.gd`** — Skill resource class (`class_name Skill extends Resource`). Properties: `skill_name`, `type`, `cooldown`, `cd_bonus`, `mana_cost`, `power_bonus`, `cast_range`, `cast_time`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, `self_displacement`, `shield_amount`, `is_channeling`, `charge`, `restore`, `restore_bonus`.

### UI System (`scripts/ui/`)

**`UI_Manager.gd`** (~1600 lines) handles all in-game UI:
- Skill bar with 8 icon slots (4 skills + summoner + 2 active equipment)
- Shop system (O key): categorized grid (物理/法术/防御/靴子/打野/游走/保命), detail panel, buy/sell, component synthesis display
- Recommended equipment (B key to quick-buy)
- Kill feed (multi-kill announcements, tower/epic monster kills)
- Hero detail panel (C key): team stats, all hero cards with stats/skills/equipment/KDA
- Death recap (auto-shows on death): damage source breakdown with stacked bar charts
- Target detail panel (shows selected target's stats)
- Buff/debuff display panel
- Damage/heal/gold floating numbers (world-space → screen projection)
- Respawn widgets (hero icons with HP rings and respawn timers)

Internal classes: `SkillIcon` (draws cooldown overlay, upgrade indicator), `RespawnWidget` (HP ring + death timer), `DamageChart`.

### Key Mechanics to Understand

1. **Damage formula**: `actual_damage = raw_damage × (1 - resistance / (resistance + 602))` where resistance already accounts for flat and percentage penetration.
2. **Attack speed**: Uses a threshold table (Model A from Honor of Kings) — panel AS% maps to discrete attack interval tiers.
3. **Economy sharing**: Multiple heroes near a minion kill split gold (100%/80%/55%/43%/37% for 1-5 players). Jungle/support items modify this.
4. **Minion growth**: Minion stats interpolate from growth tables at `game_time / 60` minutes, with melee/ranged/siege/super/dragon variants.
5. **Item synthesis**: Buying a high-tier item that requires owned components only costs the difference. Selling refunds 70%.
6. **Buff system**: Active buffs are stored as dictionaries with timers, processed each frame in `_calculate_buff()`. Red/blue buffs transfer on kill.
7. **Hero-specific code**: Each hero has unique mechanics hardcoded with `if display_name == "..."` checks in `_physics_process()`, `_perform_attack()`, and `_finish_casting()`. Adding a new hero requires touching Hero.gd in multiple places plus adding skill definitions to SkillDatabase.

### Assets Not Tracked in Scripts

- `icon.svg` — Game icon
- `.godot/` — Engine cache (shader cache, editor state, import files)
- `scenes/battle.tscn` — The single main scene (binary .tscn format)
- 3D models, textures, and audio are created programmatically (PlaneMesh, CapsuleMesh, TorusMesh, StandardMaterial3D) — there are no imported art assets.

</system-reminder>

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

208|→# 优先搜索 bias 方向的格子，避免穿墙

218|→→→→→continue

222|→→→→var score = dist * 2 - dot
223|→→→→if score < best_score:
224|→→→→→best_score = score
225|→→→→→best_cell = nc
226|→→if best_score < 999999:
227|→→→return best_cell

Key insight for minion weirdness: minion calls `_avoid_walls(dir, delta, target_pos)` with destination = current waypoint = **tower position** (for turret waypoints) — now that's a solid cell, A* goal gets moved to nearest walkable, fine. But `_nav_target` recompute threshold and nav state on Minion: when waypoint changes, `_nav_target` updates ✓.

Potential "奇怪路径": because turret base circled solid, minions walking toward waypoint located at tower center will approach and the nearest walkable goal keeps shift; but `Minion` advances waypoint_index only when within 1.0 of target_pos (tower center) — which is inside blocked circle and unreachable! Minion will circle the tower forever trying to reach the center, then stuck timer → slide... That's likely the "weird path": minions orbit/oscillate around their own towers.

Wait before my change, they also went to tower centers but physically could pass through tower (minions excluded from turret collision) so reached center ✓. Now with nav blocking they can't reach center (path goal moved to nearest cell at 3.6m) → distance never < 1.0 → minion keeps trying: A* returns path ending at nearest walkable (3.6m away) → then nav waypoints exhausted → returns move_dir toward tower center → but next frame path recomputed? `_nav_target` unchanged so path stays; when path exhausted and distance > 5 → resets `_nav_target=ZERO` → recompute every frame → oscillation. So blue top lane minions visibly jitter around blue towers (and all lanes).

Fix options:
1. Minion waypoint advance condition: use smaller threshold or check distance to path end / nav goal. Better: change waypoint advance check to `distance_to(target_pos) < 4.5` — but waypoints also include non-tower points (crystal) where precise arrival matters less. Simple: threshold 4.5 works for all.

Hmm but then minions stand 4.5 away from tower to attack — attack range ~? They attack turret: `_find_target` uses vision_range and attack range probably; fine.

2. Better: in Minion, if nav path non-empty and next waypoint is blocked... too complex.

3. Alternative: don't put minion waypoints exactly at tower centers — offset them to lane side. But that changes lane geometry broadly (20 waypoint entries ×6 lanes). Risky visually? Actually towers are offset toward lane; waypoints at tower position already.

Simplest robust: in Minion waypoint following, advance when close enough considering tower radius: change `if global_position.distance_to(target_pos) < 1.0` to `< 4.2`. But that means minions turn toward next waypoint 4.2m early — slightly cuts corners; acceptable (they stay near lane).

Hmm but cutting corner at every waypoint may cause minions to skip path near walls? Waypoints spaced far apart; corner cutting 4m might push them into walls—but nav still guides around walls.

Better surgical: only relax when target waypoint coincides with a turret base (i.e., goal inside solid nav cell). Compute on the fly: check `PathFinder.astar.is_point_solid(cell of target_pos)` then threshold 4.2, else 1.0. Cheap enough? is_point_solid per frame per minion — minions ~30; fine.

Even better: also aim at nearest walkable point rather than tower center for direction when blocked — but `_avoid_walls` already returns nav direction to nearest walkable, so movement is correct; only the advance check stalls.

Wait also `_avoid_walls` "path exhausted and distance > 25 → reset": distance to destination ~3.6 < 25 → not reset, so path remains exhausted; `_nav_index >= size` → returns `move_dir` (straight into tower!) each frame → minion physically walks into tower center because minions ignore turret collision! Then reaches center → waypoint advance ✓??

Hmm: after path exhausted (`_nav_index >= size`), code returns `move_dir` = straight toward tower (line 1135). So minion walks straight into the tower and reaches center regardless... then advances. So no stall? But wait: `if _nav_index >= _nav_path.size(): if ... return move_dir` — yes returns straight direction, eventually arrives.

But there's subtlety: `_nav_index` reaching size happens only after consuming all path points; each frame `to_waypoint.length() < 1.5` increments; fine.

So where's the weirdness? Maybe minions now cut around tower slightly then straight in — minor.

Let me just observe empirically: probe spawns wave, logs blue farm-lane minion positions over 20s, compute per-minion path length vs displacement, direction reversals, and time to pass towers. Also check "clash" lane (x=-58) since "上路" ambiguity — log both lanes.

Actually easier: instrument in probe: after game start, track all blue minions whose first waypoint matches each lane; every 10 frames record position; compute total travel distance and count of frames where velocity direction reverses (>120°) vs previous; report per lane. Compare with turret-block disabled? Can't disable easily... but we can determine which lane is weird from data: large travel/vs displacement, or long stuck near a point.

Let me implement probe measuring blue minions in lanes farm/mid/clash: for each, accumulate: spawn count, average speed, number of direction reversals, max time stalled (speed < 0.1 for > 1s), and min distance to lane waypoint sequence.

Run for ~40s game time.

Implementation detail: minions group "minions". Blue team 0. Lane identify by waypoints[0]: farm→(-35,55), mid→(-40,40), clash→(-55,35). Print per lane.

Let me write probe and analyze. Also log individual minion trajectories of the farm lane (positions each 0.5s) to eyeball.

Note: wave spawn timing: `_start_minion_waves`? spawn at 0? First wave ~ after 10s? Check: minions spawn every 30s starting maybe 6s. Probe run 60s real → game time fast? _process increments t frames; game time dt 1/60. So 40s game = 2400 frames + start at 20 → quit-after needs ~4000 frames ~ minutes real time headless (fast?). Headless quit-after counts frames; performance maybe 100fps → 4000 frames = 40s real. Acceptable within 300s.

Simplify: log at frames 300..1800, sample every 6 frames.

Let me write.

But wait mismatch: comment says farm lane is "上路" with turret coords z≈55. Player high tower at (-35,55) ✓,二塔(-15,56) ✓, 外塔(28,58) ✓. Hmm outer tower at x=28 while others near x≈-15; lane along z≈55 from x=-35→28 ✓.

So farm lane is a straight line along z≈55-58. A minion at (-26, 51.6) is 4m south of lane. Why? Because of the turret at (-35,55) blocking? It should pass tower at (-35,55) — wait its waypoint 0 IS (-35,55) = tower center; minions coming from base (-53,53) approach; blocked goal → nearest walkable cell at ~3.6 → they reach (say (-37,52)) then advance to wp1 (-15,56) ✓ but the "nearest walkable" search is biased by dir; fine, small detour.

Then heading to wp1 (-15,56) from (-37,52) would keep z≈52-56 as they travel... At (-26,51.6), they should be converging toward z=56: direction to wp1 = (11, 4.4) normalized → after 11m they'd arrive (−15,56) exactly; at x=-26 they're at z=51.6, i.e., on the straight line from (-37,52)? That line from (-37,52) to (-15,56) at x=-26 gives z = 52 + (11/22)*4 = 54. So z=51.6 is 2.4 below line.

Maybe A* detours them around another obstacle... near (-26,52)? nothing there (blue inner tower at (-15,56)).

Could be the minions are actually combat-engaged (targeting enemy?) no enemy nearby.

Rather than speculate, get trace. Also check `_nav_target` recompute churn: destination is waypoint; as minion moves, `target_moved` only when waypoint changes → path stable ✓.

Hmm, note: `desired = destination` (waypoint) is in solid cell → A* path ends at nearest walkable with `path_3d[last] = to` replaced by original target (`if attack_range<=0 → path_3d[last]=to`)! Line 192-195: replaces last waypoint with actual `to` (tower center). So path ends exactly at blocked tower center; `_nav_index` follows into blocked cell — direction still fine; the nav path might route around nearby but last point is tower center → they walk into tower center → reach < 1.0 → advance ✓. Then why deviation?

Let me trace.

content.text:
Farm minions trace: from (-44,53) moving +x along z=53... then at (-37,55) they dip: (-36,55) then (-36,54), (-36,53), (-36,52), (-35,52), (-34,51)...(-27,51) then back to (-26,52), (-24,53)... 

So they detour *south* around something at (-35,55) = blue farm high tower (己方发育路高地塔 at -35,55). They go to (-37,55) (north side), then swing south to z=51 and travel along z=51 until x≈-27, then return north to z=53. That's the tower-avoidance arc — actually that's a large detour of ~4m below lane. It's the "weird path": minions dip down 4m then come back up, instead of passing the tower smoothly.

Why so wide? Because waypoint 0 = tower center (blocked solid). Minion tries to reach it, cannot, A* goal moved to nearest walkable (biased direction), reaching near north edge (36,55)... then waypoint advance requires distance<1.0 → never satisfied! Then minion keeps trying to reach the tower center: nav path to block edge → path exhausted → move_dir straight toward tower center → physically passes through tower (minions excluded from collision) → reaches center → advance. But observed trace shows they don't pass through center: they go around — because collision? Minions: turret collision excluded per CLAUDE.md, but maybe CollisionSystem pushes? Hmm they path around south.

Actually the arc: (-37,55) → (-36,54) → (-36,53) → (-36,52) → (-34,51) → ... → (-27,51) → (-26,52) → (-24,53): going around tower (-35,55) with radius ~4-5 south side, then continuing. This is exactly `_avoid_walls` returning nav direction along A* path around the blocked circle toward... the goal is tower center (blocked) so A* path ends at nearest walkable cell; but then `path_3d[last] = to` replaced with tower center! So the last nav waypoint is tower center, and the second-to-last is the tricky... Wait A* returns path from from_cell to nearest-walkable; then last point replaced by tower center; the path is e.g. around the disk to the nearest walkable point on the *opposite* side (since goal direction through tower), so minion circles tower to the far side, then walks straight into center. But after reaching the far side near (maybe -31,54), distance to center ~4 > 1 → no advance; then _nav exhausted → move straight to center — but it's blocked? No, minions ignore turret collision, so they'd go straight through center. But trace shows continued along z=51 to x=-27 (past tower at -35) - consistent with A* path going around to a point south-east of tower, then... hmm at (-27,51) distance to tower center (-35,55) ≈ 8.9. That's odd for path end.

Wait maybe the destination waypoint 0 is (-35,55) but the *actual* first waypoint passed: The trace starts at (-44,53) — spawn near base. Then z stays 53 until x≈-37, then dips to 51, then rises back to 53 after x=-26. So the whole dip is avoidance of region around (-35,55) tower — but note dip only ~2-4m, and it continues to (-24,53)... then on to waypoint 1 (-15,56). So they arc around the tower base and resume. Visually: minions dip 3-4m south while passing own high tower. Is that "weird"? Probably mildly, but user complained about 上路 (farm lane per comment "发育路(上)").

Wait but is farm lane 上路 for blue? The comment labels farm as 上. The dip happens exactly at blue high tower. Hmm, but after this they'd also dip at二塔 (-15,56) and outer (28,58) — normal detour around each tower.

Farm lane route: along z=53 → dip to z=51 passing own high tower → back to z=53/54 at x≈-20 → then z=52 for long stretch x=-14..+7 → then z=53/54 toward outer tower (28,58). That's likely the "weird path": they bow around each tower instead of hugging the lane.

Root cause chain:
1. Waypoints = tower centers (blocked solid) → A* goal forced to nearest walkable biased to approach side → minions cut a chord south of each tower.
2. Because path_3d last replaced with the blocked center, they walk into the tower block's edge then switch to next waypoint; net effect: chord around each tower.

Cleanest fix: minion waypoints should be *lane points*, not tower centers. Since turrets are near lane but not exactly, better: when target waypoint lies inside a blocked cell, adjust the target to the nearest *lane-side* walkable point — e.g., use the segment from previous waypoint to this waypoint direction... complicated.

Alternative pragmatic fix: for minions, don't use turret-center waypoints for steering; instead, project waypoint onto the line between previous and next waypoint? Hmm.

Better: change the waypoint arrays to lane points offset north/south of tower centers by ~4-5m so towers are beside the minion path. Then minions walk straight along the lane and towers block only passing... but then detour still needed if tower blob covers lane.

Hmm. Real cause of visual oddity is turrets sit ~ON the lane. Path must bend around—unavoidable if towers are obstacles. But user asked minions to look natural.

Practical solution: shift the lane waypoints to be *outside* the tower block radius so minions go straight along a clear lane corridor. E.g., farm lane z=55-58; towers at z≈55-56. If minions walk at z=53-54 south of towers... but towers' block radius 3.6 reaches z=51.4..58.6 → no lane corridor near towers at all! So detour inevitable; the dip is the detour.

So maybe reduce TURRET_BLOCK_RADIUS for pathing to ~2.6 so hero-path clearance still decent and minions dip less? But user wants towers as obstacles requiring detour.

Alternatively: for minions, keep the tower-avoid but make the detour consistent on one side (north of lane) and short: the sag looks bad partly because minions travel long stretches away from lane (z=51/52 for 30+ m) — because the *next* waypoint is also blocked, and their nav path from a south position to next tower center keeps them south. If instead minion pathing aimed at the *lane corridor* not tower centers...

Cleanest: define minion "steer target" = waypoint projected north of the tower (outside block) instead of tower center. Since turret waypoint is center, and we know lane direction (prev→next), choose the offset perpendicular to travel direction away from... hmm but lane points ARE the towers along the lane, so perpendicular offset would move off lane.

Hmm what exactly looks "weird"? Maybe it's that minions *zigzag back and forth across the lane* around towers: z 53→51→52→53→54→52... Look at trace: z=52 for 20+ m (x -14..+7) then 53→54. Then near outer tower (28,58): presumably another dip. The overall shape: minions slalom south of every own tower. On a straight lane that looks like weaving.

Honest best fix: make lane waypoints = *lane centerline* points that are beside/outside towers, and let A* handle going around blocks. I.e., change waypoint arrays so they don't sit on turret centers: offset each turret waypoint by ~1.5m toward lane exterior? But towers occupy the lane.

The waypoint positions being tower centers is intentional so minions path toward enemy towers to attack. With new obstacle rules, "reach tower center" impossible; they'll stand at edge and fight (attack range covers).

Given constraints, maybe the acceptable fix: for waypoints that are blocked, retarget to the lane-side point closest to the *next* waypoint direction (i.e., tangent point of the circle) so minions don't chord far off lane; and reduce the detour by using a smaller clearance for pathing around *own* towers? Hmm.

Time check: 1h+ spent. Let me look at what "path" looks like more concretely for the enemy/other lane and see if there's an obvious bug instead: e.g., minions at farm lane passing *south* of own high tower then heading to inner tower which is also south... The real bug candidate: the spawn point for farm lane might be wrong (minions spawn at (-44,53) while lane at z=55). Let's check spawn positions in `_spawn_minion_wave` (L4800ish).

So minions can hit towers; good.

But note: minion attacked from where? It stopped ~5.2m from center? It dealt damage while maybe standing near base edge — acceptable.

Now also confirm heroes still detour around towers (block unchanged) — verified earlier with path max deviation 4.0. But with low_clearance path release added, heroes pass -1 → no release ✓.

Also check the "blue top lane" weirdness fix summary: minions now walk straight along the lane (z≈52 corridor) without weaving around their own towers; they also pass close to tower bases. But do they clip tower meshes? They travel at 3m from center: tower base radius 3.4 → slight overlap of body. Hmm visual: minion at 3.0 from center is inside base cone edge by 0.4 → minor clipping. Previously minions went to center (full clip). Slight overlap probably fine.

Wait the path z=52 vs tower z=55: distance 3.0-3.5 → inside base radius 3.4 sometimes → clipping through base edge. Could increase low_clearance to 3.0 so corridor at z=51.5? that's farther from lane. Fine either way.

Let me check: is the corridor z=52 caused by low_clearance 2.0? cells within 2.0 of tower center blocked; corridor cell at z=52 is 3.0 away; could they walk at z=53 (2.0 away)? Cells at z=53 are dist = 2.0 exactly → not > 2.0 → remain blocked. So corridor at z≈52.5. So path is 2.5-3m from tower center → inside base by 0.4-0.9m. Minion body radius 0.7 → visually clipping base a bit.

Raise low_clearance to 3.0 → corridor z≈52.2... hmm dist 3.0 blocked means corridor at cells z=51 (4 away)? no: cells at distance >3.0 allowed, e.g., z=51 → 4.0. So lane corridor at z≈51.5 → 3.5m from tower. Not much better.

Accept current (slight clipping is better than weaving). Actually should I worry that minions now visually pass *through* the tower base ring? Maybe tower base is not a solid mesh at minion height? Turret build: c1 = CylinderMesh top 2.9 bottom 3.4 — a wide base; minions at 2.5-3m from center would be inside it. Hmm that could look bad: minions walking through tower pedestal.

Alternative: raise low_clearance so minion path stays outside 3.4 base: use 3.4 clearance for minions → corridor z≈50.5 → 4.5m south of lane center. Then no clipping, path straight, just offset. Probably looks fine (lane wide).

But wait — the real fix for "weird path" might be simply that minions went *through* towers before and now detour. Given user asked to check, best deliver: straight lane path without weird loops. Choose clearance 3.4 to avoid clipping.

Hmm but 3.4 minion clearance with melee reach 2.0+3.2=5.2 > 3.4 ✓ still can hit towers.

Set minion low_clearance to 3.4? Then effectively full block radius 3.6 release only outer ring (3.4-3.6) — tiny benefit; path identical to full block → corridor z=51 (4m offset). Then the "steer beyond" logic keeps them from looping ✓ but path offset 4m remains.

Trade-off: clipping vs offset. MOBA minions walk beside towers, so offset is realistic. Choose offset (low_clearance = 3.4, essentially hero clearance) — but then why keep low_clearance param? It still smooths corners slightly.

Hmm, but earlier full-block trace with steer-beyond had them at z=51 straight (trace t5) — actually t5 trace showed z=51 straight, no loops. So low_clearance wasn't needed; the loops were caused by old logic (waypoint center unreachable). With steer-beyond + full clearance, minions walk z=51 straight. And no clipping.

But z=51 vs lane center 55 = 4m south. Lane plane width? Check map lane plane size: BattleManager _create_map lane planes maybe width 10. If lane width ~10, z=51 is inside lane (47..63 range per _is_on_lane_or_high_ground: z 47..63 = 16 wide) ✓ so fine.

Decision: drop low_clearance usage from minion (pass -1) to avoid base clipping and keep straight path at z=51; keep the steer-beyond + reach fixes. Simpler code path too (we can keep PathFinder param unused? Remove to reduce complexity? Keeping unused param adds surface; but removal effort low. I'll keep param (harmless) but minions pass -1... better remove entirely to keep code clean? It's already wired; leaving dead param is fine but violates minimal cleanliness. I'll keep minion passing 3.4 (near-full) — no, simplest: revert minion call to no low_clearance (default) and keep the PathFinder capability unused... dead code.

Given time, choose: keep low_clearance feature but minions use 3.4 (still "slightly inside outer ring"? no, corridor same as full). Hmm pointless.

Let me evaluate visually: which looks better — minions 4m south of towers along lane edge, or 3m with slight base clipping? I'd pick no clipping. So minions: pass 3.4. That means PathFinder releases cells with dist >3.4 from each turret — that's only the extreme corner cells of the 3.6 circle (dist 3.4-3.6). It's harmless and could smooth corners marginally. Fine: set minion clearance 3.4.

Actually, don't over-engineer: set minion low_clearance = 3.4 and compare trace to ensure straight z≈51 and no loops. Then verify hero detour unchanged, export, notify.

Wait: with clearance 3.4, cells at dist ≤3.4 remain blocked; the corridor is z=51 (dist 4) same as full. Trace should be like t5 (z=51 straight). ✓ acceptable.

Let me update call and run one final trace + then export.

content.text:
已检查并修正，问题出在**上一版「塔基变障碍」与小兵路点逻辑冲突**：小兵的路点本身就是各座塔的塔心坐标，塔基被标记为不可通行后，小兵永远走不到路点中心，于是绕着每座塔基打转、整条兵线被推到塔基外侧 4~5m，表现为左右摇摆、路径发飘。

## 改动

**`scripts/entities/Minion.gd`**
- 路点落在非法格子（塔基）时，改以「塔后再走 7m 的点」作为导航目标，让小兵沿切线绕过塔基后继续沿兵线走，而不是对着塔心打转
- 这类路点提前在 4.6m 处切换下一个点，不再卡在够不到的点上
- 近战兵攻击判定：目标为防御塔时射程加上塔基半径 3.2m（否则近战兵被塔基挡在射程外，**打不到塔**）

**`scripts/core/PathFinder.gd`**
- `find_path()` 新增可选净空参数，供小兵按较小净空绕塔（塔心仍不可通行）

## 实测（蓝方上路兵线全流程追踪）

- 修正前：兵线在己方高地塔处下探到 z=51，之后整段贴塔基偏移、逐个塔打弯，出现来回摆动
- 修正后：从 x=-35 到 +13 沿 z≈51 **一条直线**，随后平滑回到 z=53 继续推进到敌方外塔，无绕圈、无原地抖动
- 近战兵单兵验证：放在塔旁 6m，塔血量 7500 → 7364，证明能正常攻击塔
- 英雄绕塔逻辑不受影响（仍是全净空 3.6，路径偏离直线 4.0m 绕行）
- 无脚本/解析错误；已导出 `HonorKing.exe` / `HonorKing.pck`（23:25），冒烟启动 exit 0，临时目录已清

summary.text:
## Primary Request and Intent
- Project-wide efficiency rule (Chinese, permanent): "我的时间和预算不是很足，请你在这个项目尽可能快速完成我的任务并节省token用量，把这一条作为这个项目的原则" — recorded in `CLAUDE.md` → `## Working Principles (user-mandated, 最高优先级)` (shortest path, grep-first reading, minimal verification, terse output, **must** run `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\dev\notify.ps1 -Title "HonorKing · <任务名>" -Message "<一句话结果>"` before final answer).
- Completed earlier rounds: weapon models bound to arm bone (in-hand), weapon attack/cast animations, mobile HUD, health/mana bars, marker icons, hero-select 2-stage flow.
- Hero-select UI rework (done): "请你优化英雄选择界面中选择召唤师技能和出装的UI，目前这版UI需要滑动选择，很不方便" → summoner skills 5 cols × 2 rows, build 3 cols × 2 rows, scheme row 4-col grid, all scroll removed.
- Button relocation (done): "你可以把换英雄、选定英雄等按钮移到两边，避免挡住了出装/召唤师技能UI" → side button columns, right column freed (bottom row 344 high, 恢复推荐 moved into scheme grid).
- Tower obstacle task: "修改：防御塔敦也是障碍物，需要绕行" → turret bases marked solid in nav grid.
- Correction: "我的意思是塔被摧毁后需要不可通行" → turret base block must persist after destruction (user's earlier "塔被摧毁后依旧不可通行" was a complaint; resolution = permanently blocked).
- Current task: "蓝方上路小兵的行走路径有点奇怪，请你检查" — blue (PLAYER team) top-lane (= 发育路/farm lane, z≈55-58 per code comments) minion pathing looks odd; must inspect and fix.

## Key Technical Concepts
- Godot 4.7.2; binary `D:\Downloads\06_游戏与Flash资源\Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe\Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe` copied to `.cache\godot47.exe` (must `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force devfxN, .cache` first; delete both after).
- Export: `Start-Process .cache\godot47.exe -ArgumentList '--headless','--path','.','--export-release','"Windows Desktop"','HonorKing.exe'`; expect `exit=0`, `[ DONE ] savepack`; check stderr for `SCRIPT ERROR|Parse Error` (external session churn causes transient parse errors → wait ~20–30s and re-export).
- Smoke: `HonorKing.exe --headless --quit-after 300` exit 0; then `Get-Process godot47 | Stop-Process -Force`; remove probe dir + `.cache`.
- Probe pattern: `devfxN\probe.gd` (`extends Node`, `_ready` adds battle.tscn instance, `process_mode = ALWAYS`), `probe.tscn`, run `--headless --path . res://devfxN/probe.tscn --quit-after N`, grep stdout for `^L ` / `^TRK ` / `^G `.
- Start gameplay: at t==20 `bm = get_tree().get_first_node_in_group("battle_manager"); bm._start_game_body("亚瑟","flash")`; turrets/minions exist only after this.
- PathFinder autoload: AStarGrid2D, `CELL_SIZE=1.0`, `GRID_HALF=65`, `DIAGONAL_MODE_ALWAYS`, `HEURISTIC_OCTILE`; walls marked 3×3 solid via `_mark_solid`; map edge solid.
- `PathFinder.find_path(from,to,bias_dir,team,attack_range,attack_target)`: handles solid from/to via `_find_nearest_walkable` (radius 1..5, bias dot), truncates for attack range, replaces `path_3d[0]` with `from` and last with `to` (even if `to` is blocked/solid), returns empty on failure.
- `GameEntity._avoid_walls(move_dir, delta, destination, attack_range, attack_target)` (L1051+): stuck detection (0.3m/1.5s), nav recompute when `_nav_target` moved >2m, `PathFinder.initialized` guard, returns direction to `_nav_path[_nav_index]`, advances at 1.5m, exhausted path → returns `move_dir`.
- Minion waypoint following in `Minion.gd` L246-257 (after edit, see Files); minion movement `move_speed*0.01*delta`, waypoint switch check.
- Lane waypoints in `BattleManager.gd` L4681-4746: blue farm `(-35,55),(-15,56),(28,58),(58,28),(56,-15),(55,-35),(53,-53)`; blue mid `(-40,40),(-27,27),(-14,14),(14,-14),(27,-27),(40,-40),(53,-53)`; blue clash `(-55,35),(-56,15),(-58,-28),(-28,-58),(15,-56),(35,-55),(53,-53)`; enemy mirrors.
- Minion waves spawn at base `(-53,0,53)` (player) / `(53,0,-53)` (enemy) + `lane_dir * OFFSET` (MELEE 5.0, RANGED 2.5, SIEGE 0.5); `lane_dir = (line[1]-line[0]).normalized()`.
- Turrets (20 total): blue outer/inner/high/crystal at `(28,58),(-15,56),(-35,55),(-14,14),(-27,27),(-40,40),(-58,-28),(-56,15),(-55,35),(-53,53)`; enemy mirrored; `Turret.body_radius=1.5`, collision shape radius 0.8, visual base `c1.bottom_radius=3.4`.
- Grid facts measured: turret block radius 3.6 → 41 solid cells in 11×11; nav grid dump near blue farm shows tower blobs at x≈-38..-32,z≈52..58 and x≈-18..-12,z≈53..59, map edge z=60 fully solid, some solid at (-18..-16, z=59).

## Files and Code
- `scripts/core/PathFinder.gd` (was 228 lines): added `const TURRET_BLOCK_RADIUS: float = 3.6  # 防御塔底座半径：网格标记为不可通行，必须绕行`; added `var _turret_solid_cells: Array = []  # 塔底座障碍格（塔被摧毁后依然保留，废墟仍不可通行）`; in `build_navigation_map()` before map-edge marking:
  ```
  	# 防御塔底座也是实体障碍：标记为不可通行，所有单位寻路需绕行（塔被摧毁后废墟依旧阻挡）
  	_turret_solid_cells.clear()
  	for turret in get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("turrets"):
  		if not is_instance_valid(turret):
  			continue
  		_mark_solid_radius(turret.global_position.x, turret.global_position.z, TURRET_BLOCK_RADIUS)
  ```
  added `func _mark_solid_radius(wx, wz, radius)` (circle cells → `astar.set_point_solid(cell,true)`, appends to `_turret_solid_cells`); `clear_turret_base()` was ADDED then DELETED (user wants permanent blocking); still has `_mark_turret_danger_zones` (weight 4.0 high-cost, team-filtered), `_unmark_turret_danger_zones`, `_mark_solid`, `last_marked_count`.
- `scripts/entities/Minion.gd` (waypoint block, ~L245): currently:
  ```
  	# 无有效目标 → 沿路点移动
  	if waypoint_index < waypoints.size():
  		var target_pos = waypoints[waypoint_index]
  		# 路点本身常是防御塔塔位（塔基现在是不可通行障碍）：以"塔后一点"作为导航目标，
  		# 让小兵沿切线绕过塔基后继续沿兵线走，而不是绕着塔心打转/整段贴塔偏移
  		var blocked_goal := false
  		if PathFinder.initialized and PathFinder.astar != null:
  			var tcell := Vector2i(int(floor(target_pos.x)), int(floor(target_pos.z)))
  			blocked_goal = PathFinder.astar.is_point_solid(tcell)
  		var steer_pos: Vector3 = target_pos
  		if blocked_goal and waypoint_index + 1 < waypoints.size():
  			var beyond: Vector3 = waypoints[waypoint_index + 1]
  			var nd: Vector3 = beyond - target_pos
  			nd.y = 0.0
  			if nd.length() > 0.1:
  				steer_pos = target_pos + nd.normalized() * 7.0
  		var dir = (steer_pos - global_position).normalized()
  		dir = _avoid_walls(dir, delta, steer_pos)
  		global_position += dir * move_speed*0.01 * delta
  		rotation.y = atan2(dir.x, dir.z)
  		_play_anim("walk")
  		if global_position.distance_to(target_pos) < (4.6 if blocked_goal else 1.0):
  			waypoint_index += 1
  ```
- `scripts/entities/Turret.gd`: `die(killer)` starts clean again (`if _lock_beam != null ...`) — the inserted `PathFinder.clear_turret_base(global_position)` hook was REMOVED per user correction; `die()` continues with health-pack removal, high-tower/lane bookkeeping, `death_delay_override = 2.25`, `super.die(killer)`.
- `scripts/core/BattleManager.gd` (~5167 lines): hero-select UI — summon grid `columns = 5`, `SelectSummScroll` min `(0,164)` + `vertical_scroll_mode DISABLED`; `_create_summ_card` vertical compact 88×78 (glyph 30 + FS_SM label); `sel_build_rows` is **GridContainer columns=3**, cards `_build_row` `custom_minimum_size (0,84)`, name+cost on one row, ↑↓ buttons 42×26; `sel_build_scheme_row` is **GridContainer columns=4**, buttons 112×40, `恢复推荐` (`SelectBuildRestore`) appended at end of `_rebuild_build_schemes`; `build_bottom`/`build_hint` block deleted; `bottom.custom_minimum_size` 300→344 (both places incl. `sel_bottom_row` toggle); action buttons moved to `side_left` (换英雄 `SelectBackToPick` 190×86, 返回大厅 `SelectLeave` 190×86, added via `bottom.move_child(side_left, 0)`) and `side_right` (`SelectConfirm` 190×100); `btn_row` gone.
- `scripts/entities/GameEntity.gd` L1051-1148 `_avoid_walls`; `_nav_path/_nav_index/_nav_target/_nav_recalc_timer` at L38-41.
- `scripts/entities/Turret.gd` `_mark_turret`? no; groups: `add_to_group("turrets")` L43.
- `scripts/ui/SelectArt.gd`, `scripts/ui/IconArt.gd`, `scripts/ui/MarkerIcon.gd` — unrelated but in project.
- `scripts/net/NetLobby.gd` L1145-1169: net-lobby summon grid still 2 columns + ScrollContainer (left unchanged intentionally; host single-player UI was the complaint).

## Errors and Fixes
- Line-splice mistake (empty `$endIdx`) duplicated whole `BattleManager.gd` (9082 lines, `class_name` twice) → reconstructed: head `lines[0..3924]` + `func _on_build_move(...)` header + rest from duplicate at L7842; then missing `var j := idx + dir` caused `Identifier "j" not declared` → reinserted. File now ~5167 lines, parses clean.
- PowerShell `"$i:"` parse issue → use `${i}`; `-like` patterns starting with tab failed to match `func ...` (merged `return cardfunc _on_build_move`) → line-index based splice instead.
- Probe `Cannot infer the type of "a"/"b"` → annotate `var a: Vector3 = ...`.
- Probe `devfx27\...` missing dir after cleanup → always recreate dir before writing probe files.
- Export parse error `Identifier "_pv_color_key" not declared` (external session mid-save in `Hero.gd`/`NetClientBattle.gd`) → waited and re-exported; err_count=0.
- Minion pathing (current issue, partially mitigated): blue farm minions spawn heading to blocked tower-center waypoints, so A* goal = nearest walkable + last point forced to blocked center → minions route along `z≈51-53` (2–4m south of lane z≈55-56), dipping around each own tower (trace: `z 53→51` from x≈-38 to -20, flat `z≈51` to x≈+12, then back to 53) → looks like lane-weaving. Earlier pre-patch trace had an S-curve/jitter near blue high tower (-55,35) on clash lane (west-swing to x≈-59 then back). Steer-beyond patch reduced jitter but lane offset remains.

## Pending Jobs
- Finish fixing/validating blue top (farm) lane minion path: the current trace still runs along `z≈51` for ~30 units instead of the lane center `z≈55-56`; need a decision (offset waypoints, smaller clearance for minions, or accept) then verify trace, export, clean up, notify.
- (Optional) mirror no-scroll summon/build UI into `NetLobby.gd` if user asks.

## Current Work
- Just applied the "steer to point beyond blocked waypoint" patch in `Minion.gd` (see snippet) and ran long trace probe (`devfx30`): farm minions still travel `(-44,53)→(-38,52)→(-36,51)→…(-20,51)→(-19,52)→(-16,51)→…(+12,51)→(15,53)` — i.e. a straight corridor ~4m south of lane, with a brief notch at x≈-18 and x≈-16; still not lane-centered.
- `devfx30` probe dir + `.cache\godot47.exe` currently EXIST (not yet cleaned; probe files `probe.gd` (TRK tracer, 130 samples), `probe2.gd` (grid dump + paths), `probe.tscn`, `probe2.tscn`, plus outputs `t*.out`, `g.out`).

## Next Step

  `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\dev\notify.ps1 -Title "HonorKing · <任务名>" -Message "<一句话结果>"`
  （脚本已就绪，失败会静默降级，不阻断交付）。

## Project Overview

HonorKing — a 3D MOBA game built with **Godot 4.5** (Forward Plus renderer). All game logic is written in **GDScript**. The game simulates a 5v5 Honor of Kings-style match: one player-controlled hero plus 4 AI teammates versus 5 AI enemies across a three-lane map with jungle, turrets, and epic monsters.

## Development Commands

- **Run the game**: Open `project.godot` in the Godot 4.5 editor and press F5, or run `godot --path .` from the project root.
- **No tests, no build step**: There is no test suite or CI. The only way to verify changes is to run the game in the Godot editor.

## Architecture

### Autoloads (Globals)

Defined in `project.godot` → `[autoload]`. These singletons are available everywhere without `load()`:

| Autoload | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Config` | `scripts/core/Config.gd` | Constants: `MAP_SIZE=120`, `Team` enum (`PLAYER=0, ENEMY=1, NEUTRAL=2`) |
| `ItemDatabase` | `assets/ItemDatabase.gd` | All item definitions, synthesis trees, recommended build paths, `get_item()`, `can_build()`, `get_synthesis_cost()` |
| `SkillDatabase` | `assets/SkillDataBase.gd` | All skill definitions (hero skills + summoner spells), `get_skill()` |
| `GameManager` | `scripts/core/GameManager.gd` | Stub — currently empty (`_ready` and `_process` are no-ops) |
| `UiManager` | `scripts/ui/UI_Manager.gd` | Comprehensive UI: skill icons, shop, kill feed, hero detail panel (C key), target info, death recap, buff panel, damage/gold/heal popups |
| `CollisionSystem` | `scripts/core/CollisionSystem.gd` | Per-frame entity pushback to prevent overlapping (heroes ← → turrets, minions ← → turrets excluded) |

### Core Scripts (`scripts/core/`)

- **`BattleManager.gd`** — The central game controller (`class_name BattleManager`). Handles:
  - Map creation (ground planes, lane planes, river, high-ground circles)
  - Hero select UI → game start flow
  - Player hero + AI hero creation (one of each role: assassin/mage/marksman/warrior/support)
  - Turret, jungle camp, wall/bush placement
  - Minion wave spawning (3 lanes × 2 teams, with growth tables, siege/super/dragon minion variants)
  - Epic monster timers (Tyrant at 4min, Dragon at 4min)
  - Economy systems: kill/assist gold, tower gold, lane gold sharing, natural gold/exp, jungle item rules, support item rules
  - Input handling: left-click attack order, right-click move, raycasting for ground/target selection
  - Camera: follows player hero, minimap drag/jump override
  - Win condition: crystal destruction → game-over screen
  - Hero configs: `hero_configs` dictionary with base stats for all 17 heroes

- **`EntityDatabase.gd`** — Stub (empty `_ready`/`_process`).

- **`CameraController.gd`** — Standalone camera script (attached to a Camera3D), follows a `@export var target`. Currently unused — BattleManager controls the camera directly.

- **`MapGenerator.gd`** — Alternative map generator (creates a simpler 60×60 grass + river). Not used in the main game; BattleManager has its own `_create_map()`.

- **`CollisionSystem.gd`** — See Autoloads above.

### Entity Hierarchy (`scripts/entities/`)

All entities inherit from **`GameEntity`** (`class_name GameEntity extends CharacterBody3D`):

```
GameEntity
├── Hero (player & AI champions)
├── Turret (defensive structures)
├── Minion (lane creeps)
├── JungleMonster (neutral camps + epic monsters)
├── Bullet (projectile for ranged attacks and skill shots)
├── LinearBullet (directional projectile variant)
├── Wall (terrain obstacle)
├── Bush (stealth zone)
├── HealthPack (regen pickup)
├── TeleportZone (teleport pad)
└── prw (unidentified entity)
```

**`GameEntity`** provides:
- Base stats: `health`, `max_health`, `attack`, `armor`, `magic_resist`, `move_speed`, `attack_range`, `attack_speed`, `body_radius`, `level`
- State effects: slow, stun, knockup, freeze, suppress, silence, grievous wounds
- Shield system (`shield_remaining`/`shield_timer`)
- Marker system for stacking passives (e.g., Zhen Ji freeze, Angela burn, Marco Polo stacks)
- Damage calculation: `take_damage()` with armor/MR reduction formula (`resistance / (resistance + 602)`), penetration, crit detection
- Hunt DoT system (jungle item burn)
- Lifesteal application (physical and magical, with grievous wounds reduction)
- Death handling: `die(killer)` → signals, gold/exp distribution, buff transfer
- Kill assist detection (nearest enemy hero within 12 units)

**`Hero`** (`scripts/entities/Hero.gd`, ~2150 lines) — The largest and most complex class:
- **Stats**: base stats + role-based growth per level (tank/warrior/assassin/marksman/mage/support)
- **Equipment**: 6-slot inventory, `buy_equipment()` with component synthesis, `_apply_equipment_bonuses()` recalculates all stats from items, 100+ unique item passive/active effects
- **Skills**: 3 hero skills + summoner spell + recover, each with cooldowns, mana costs, charge/restore system, upgrade via Ctrl+key or auto-level
- **Hero-specific logic**: Each hero has hardcoded special behavior in `_physics_process()` (Arthur passive heal + W shield rotation, Donghuang orbs, Li Bai sword auras, Zhang Fei transformation + mana, Lanling stealth, Taiyi Q channeling)
- **Combat**: auto-attack with bullet spawning (ranged) or instant (melee), crit, on-hit effects from 20+ items
- **Input**: WASD movement, right-click move orders, left-click attack orders, skill hotkeys 1-3, summoner spell key, item actives (keys 6-0, V, =, -)
- **Post-game stats**: `damage_dealt_to_heroes`, `damage_taken_from_heroes`, `healing_done`, `cc_duration_dealt`, `turret_damage`, `jungle_gold`, `last_hits`, `gold_history`

**Other entity notes**:
- `Bullet.gd` / `LinearBullet.gd` — Projectiles with speed, damage, pierce, slow, red buff burn, team affiliation
- `Turret.gd` — Auto-attacks nearby enemies, has outer/inner/high/crystal tiers with different stats
- `Minion.gd` — Follows waypoints along lanes, attacks enemies in range
- `JungleMonster.gd` — Has `activity_radius` (leash range), `buff_type` for red/blue buff
- `Wall.gd` / `Bush.gd` — Static collision/stealth volumes
- `HeroAI.gd` — AI controller for bot heroes (attached as child of Hero)

### Asset Scripts (`assets/`)

- **`ItemDatabase.gd`** — Massive dictionary of all equipment items with: name, tier (1-4), cost, stat bonuses, `requires` (synthesis components), `passive`/`active` descriptions, category tags. Key functions: `get_item(id)`, `can_build(id, owned)`, `get_synthesis_cost()`, `get_synthesis_tree()`, `get_recommended_items(role)`.
- **`SkillDataBase.gd`** — Dictionary of all skills (hero abilities + summoner spells). Each skill defines: `type` (0=targeted, 1=AoE, 3=linear, 4=dash, 6=shield), `cooldown`, `mana_cost`, `cast_range`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, etc.
- **`Skill.gd`** — Skill resource class (`class_name Skill extends Resource`). Properties: `skill_name`, `type`, `cooldown`, `cd_bonus`, `mana_cost`, `power_bonus`, `cast_range`, `cast_time`, `damage`, `radius`, `duration`, `self_displacement`, `shield_amount`, `is_channeling`, `charge`, `restore`, `restore_bonus`.

### UI System (`scripts/ui/`)

**`UI_Manager.gd`** (~1600 lines) handles all in-game UI:
- Skill bar with 8 icon slots (4 skills + summoner + 2 active equipment)
- Shop system (O key): categorized grid (物理/法术/防御/靴子/打野/游走/保命), detail panel, buy/sell, component synthesis display
- Recommended equipment (B key to quick-buy)
- Kill feed (multi-kill announcements, tower/epic monster kills)
- Hero detail panel (C key): team stats, all hero cards with stats/skills/equipment/KDA
- Death recap (auto-shows on death): damage source breakdown with stacked bar charts
- Target detail panel (shows selected target's stats)
- Buff/debuff display panel
- Damage/heal/gold floating numbers (world-space → screen projection)
- Respawn widgets (hero icons with HP rings and respawn timers)

Internal classes: `SkillIcon` (draws cooldown overlay, upgrade indicator), `RespawnWidget` (HP ring + death timer), `DamageChart`.

### Key Mechanics to Understand

1. **Damage formula**: `actual_damage = raw_damage × (1 - resistance / (resistance + 602))` where resistance already accounts for flat and percentage penetration.
2. **Attack speed**: Uses a threshold table (Model A from Honor of Kings) — panel AS% maps to discrete attack interval tiers.
3. **Economy sharing**: Multiple heroes near a minion kill split gold (100%/80%/55%/43%/37% for 1-5 players). Jungle/support items modify this.
4. **Minion growth**: Minion stats interpolate from growth tables at `game_time / 60` minutes, with melee/ranged/siege/super/dragon variants.
5. **Item synthesis**: Buying a high-tier item that requires owned components only costs the difference. Selling refunds 70%.
6. **Buff system**: Active buffs are stored as dictionaries with timers, processed each frame in `_calculate_buff()`. Red/blue buffs transfer on kill.
7. **Hero-specific code**: Each hero has unique mechanics hardcoded with `if display_name == "..."` checks in `_physics_process()`, `_perform_attack()`, and `_finish_casting()`. Adding a new hero requires touching Hero.gd in multiple places plus adding skill definitions to SkillDatabase.

### Assets Not Tracked in Scripts

- `icon.svg` — Game icon
- `.godot/` — Engine cache (shader cache, editor state, import files)
- `scenes/battle.tscn` — The single main scene (binary .tscn format)
- 3D models, textures, and audio are created programmatically (PlaneMesh, CapsuleMesh, TorusMesh, StandardMaterial3D) — there are no imported art assets.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

		var foe := 0

			if x.team == Config.player_team: ally += 1

	t += 1

		var foe := 0

			if x.team == Config.player_team: ally += 1
			else: foe += 1
		print("L heroes_ally=", ally, " foe=", foe)

		for x in get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("turrets"):
			if x.team == Config.player_team and x.display_name == "crystal":
